results.title: Z.ai: Official Playground for High-Performance GLM Models
results.content:
Gal Dayan

#### What's great

Ran GLM-5.3 through the coding plan against a real bug in a personal project rather than a toy prompt. It found the root cause in a legacy module faster than I expected and the reasoning trace was actually readable, not just a wall of tokens. Output token usage was noticeably lower than what I'm used to from Opus for a comparable task, which matters when you're iterating a lot in one session.

#### What needs improvement [...] #### What needs improvement

The one thing that gave me pause after using it wasn't the coding quality, it was reading the launch thread afterward and seeing the model can now reason through complete exploitation chains, with open weights landing in two weeks. I'd want the safety hardening timeline to be a lot more visible up front, not something you only find by scrolling the comments.

#### vs Alternatives

Claude by Anthropic

I still default to Claude Code for anything I actually bill a client for, but for a personal project where the free tier covers it, GLM-5.3 held up well enough on this particular bug that I didn't feel like I was using a downgrade. Wouldn't swap yet on something I'm being paid to get right, but it earned a second look.

Ekaterina Tsyganova

results.title: Freebuff: Free coding agents to kill Claude, Cursor, Replit, and Devin | Product Hunt
results.content:
Mostly consolidation. I was juggling several AI subscriptions, and Freebuff lets me use one setup for coding, document generation, academic drafts, and random technical troubleshooting. It doesn't magically beat every paid tool at everything, but having the same workspace for all of my work is worth more than constantly rebuilding my workflow around the latest tool. DeepSeek V4 Flash has been my daily driver there recently, and I picked up GLM 5.2 through their bounty system.
